items.title: Fixed-design linear regression model
items.statement: A fixed-design first-moment regression model has fixed X in R^{n x p}, parameter beta in R^p, observation space R^n with its Borel sigma-algebra, and response Y with finite coordinate means E_beta[Y]=X beta. It imposes no covariance, independence, or Gaussian assumption.
items.strategy: Define the regression experiment as a parametric family of laws on the response space and state fixed-design conditioning and first-moment scope.

references.title: Statistics for Applications, Section 15: Multiple Linear Regression
references.locator: PDF pp. 1-2: fixed-design matrix model and full-rank scope; Gaussian assumptions are not imported into this first-moment definition.

references.title: Statistics: Lecture Three — Linear Models
references.locator: PDF pp. 2-4: response, predictor matrix, and fixed-design model notation.

items.title: Linear statistics on Euclidean data are Borel-measurable
items.statement: For n >= 1 and a in R^n, the map y -> a^T y from Euclidean R^n to Borel R is measurable.
items.strategy: Bound the linear functional to obtain a Lipschitz map, then use continuity to pull Borel sets back to Borel sets.

items.title: Least-squares solution set
items.statement: For X in R^{n x p} and y in R^n, define B_LS(y)=argmin_{b in R^p} ||y-Xb||_2^2. This is a set-valued definition and does not select a coefficient vector.
items.strategy: Define the full minimizer set using the Euclidean norm; the following theorem proves it is nonempty and describes its fitted vector.

references.title: Statistics for Applications, Section 15: Multiple Linear Regression
references.locator: PDF pp. 1-2: least-squares objective and normal equations.

references.locator: PDF pp. 3-4: squared-error minimization and projection interpretation.

items.title: Least-squares fitted vectors and residuals are unique
items.statement: For fixed X and y, the least-squares coefficient set is nonempty, is characterized by X^T(Xb-y)=0, and equals b0+ker X; every minimizer has the same fitted vector and residual. Its direction space ker X has dimension p-rank(X).
items.strategy: Apply the published least-squares normal-equation theorem, identify the image minimizer by orthogonal projection, and use rank-nullity for the affine solution dimension.

references.locator: PDF pp. 1-4: normal equations, fitted projection, and residual projection.

items.title: Linearly estimable contrasts in fixed-design regression
items.statement: For c in R^p, the contrast beta -> c^T beta is linearly estimable if there is a fixed a in R^n such that a^T Y is an unbiased measurable estimator of c^T beta for every beta.
items.strategy: Specialize the estimand and estimator definitions to a fixed-design regression experiment; require a deterministic linear statistic and unbiasedness for every parameter.

references.title: Statistics: Lecture Three — Linear Models
references.locator: PDF p. 5: definition of an estimable linear function by a linear unbiased estimator.

references.title: Statistics for Applications, Section 15: Multiple Linear Regression
references.locator: PDF pp. 5-6: linear contrasts and estimators under the full-rank Gaussian model.

items.title: Linear estimability is equivalent to row-space membership
items.statement: Under the fixed-design first-moment model, c^T beta is linearly estimable if and only if c is in row(X)=im(X^T), equivalently X^T a=c for some a in R^n; then a^T Y is unbiased.
items.strategy: Compute E_beta[a^T Y]=(X^T a)^T beta and use equality for every beta to identify the coefficient vector.

references.title: Statistics: Lecture Three — Linear Models
references.locator: PDF p. 5: estimability definition and row-space condition.

references.title: Statistics for Applications, Section 15: Multiple Linear Regression
references.locator: PDF pp. 5-6: linear contrast notation and full-rank consequence.

items.title: Full-rank OLS is unbiased with its classical covariance
items.statement: If X has full column rank and E_beta epsilon=0 with Cov_beta(epsilon)=sigma^2 I_n for sigma^2>0, then the unique OLS estimator is (X^T X)^{-1}X^T Y, is unbiased for beta, and has covariance sigma^2(X^T X)^{-1}. No Gaussian assumption is required.
items.strategy: Use the normal equation, prove X^T X is invertible, and apply the first- and second-moment identities to the resulting linear estimator.

references.title: Statistics: Lecture Three — Linear Models

references.title: Statistics for Applications, Section 15: Multiple Linear Regression
references.locator: PDF pp. 1-3: full-rank formula and coefficient covariance derivation; Gaussianity is not used for the moment result.

items.title: Gauss–Markov theorem for estimable contrasts
items.statement: For fixed full-column-rank X, E_beta epsilon=0, and Cov_beta(epsilon)=sigma^2 I_n with sigma^2>0, OLS estimates every contrast c^T beta with minimum variance among all linear unbiased estimators; Gaussianity is not required.
items.strategy: Represent any competing estimator as a^T Y with X^T a=c, subtract the OLS coefficient vector, and use orthogonality to cancel the covariance cross-term.

items.title: Collinear predictors can leave a contrast estimable
items.statement: For X with two identical columns, the least-squares fitted vector is unique while the coefficient vector is not; the sum contrast is linearly estimable and either single coefficient is not.
items.strategy: Compute the minimizer set and row space for the two-row design with identical columns.

items.title: Unequal error variances can make OLS fail to be BLUE
items.statement:
For every full-column-rank fixed design and every mean-zero error law with
finite second moments, OLS is the best linear unbiased estimator of every
contrast, regardless of the error covariance.
items.strategy: Use a two-observation intercept-only design with finite errors of unequal variances and exhibit a lower-variance unbiased linear estimator.

items.title: Leverage is determined by the design
items.statement: For a full-rank simple-regression design, the diagonal of the projection onto the design column space can be close to one at an extreme predictor value; this leverage value depends only on X.
items.strategy: Decompose the design column space into its orthogonal intercept and centered-predictor directions and calculate the final projection diagonal.
